assessment.name: Pica, ARFID, and Rumination Disorder Interview – ARFID Questionnaire: Informant-report (PARDI-AR-Q-Informant)
assessment.description: The Pica, ARFID, and Rumination Disorder Interview – ARFID Questionnaire (PARDI-AR-Q) Informant form is a 29-item measure for clinicians screening for avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID) in children aged 4 and over. It is completed by a parent or carer reporting on their child.

administration.instructions: The following questions are about your child's eating — some ask about how things currently are, others ask about things over the past month or the past 3 months. Please select the response that applies, or enter the information requested. Please read each question carefully. Please answer all the questions. Thank you.

source_guidance.title: PARDI-AR-Q Scoring & Interpretation
source_guidance.text:
The PARDI-AR-Q is originally described as a 32-item scale, however items 1, 2 and 3 are date, date of birth and sex, which are recorded automatically in the NovoPsych platform, therefore, NovoPsych refers to the PARDI-AR-Q as being a 29-item scale, numbering these items 1 to 29 in the order they are answered, beginning with height and weight. Question numbers on this page match the 29-item formatting.
The 29 items fall into three blocks:
1. Anthropometric items (items 1-2): the child’s height and weight (2 items). Together with age and sex, these produce BMI and growth status.
2. Diagnostic items (items 3 to 18): twelve are scored Yes = 1 / No = 0 and drive the screen; the other four (items 7, 13, 15, 17) are conditionally displayed follow-ups that are not scored (item 7 is a numeric entry for how much weight has been lost; items 13, 15, and 17 are free text).
3. Rating items scored 0 to 6 (items 19 to 29, 11 items): the severity-of-impact index (items 19 to 20) and the three subscale scores (items 21 to 29; 3 items each).
Recall periods are not fixed and vary by item, spanning current, past-month, and past-3-month timeframes.

source_guidance.title: Why doesn't the PARDI-AR-Q give a total score?
source_guidance.text: The three ARFID subscales are distinct and can occur in any combination, so combining them into a single score would obscure the distinction the measure exists to draw. A child can score high on sensory-based avoidance and low on the other two, and that subscale means something different from a child with the reverse pattern. For that reason the subscales are reported and read separately rather than combined.
